## ⚠️ Auto-merge is armed, but this will **not** merge as it stands — the ADR approval gate has zero reviews

@hotlong — you enabled auto-merge at 12:14Z. Flagging immediately rather than letting it sit looking armed, because arming it is not sufficient here and nothing will happen until one more action.

Verified just now:

| | |
|---|---|
| auto-merge | ✅ enabled (by you, `merge`) |
| reviews on this PR | **0** — none of any kind |
| `mergeable_state` | **`blocked`** |
| requested reviewer | `hotlong` |

The ADR merge gate (`scripts/check-adr-merge-approval.mjs`) requires an **APPROVED review to exist** — that is its literal rule per the 2026-08-12 ruling on #8161. With zero reviews it cannot pass, so auto-merge will wait indefinitely rather than land.

⇒ **One action unblocks it: approve this PR.** Auto-merge then does the rest.

### ⛔ Why I am not doing anything else here

This PR's own body says no AI seat merges it, queues it, or arms auto-merge on it — Prime Directive #14, because the diff touches `docs/adr/**`. **You arming auto-merge yourself supersedes that for the arming step**, and I am not second-guessing it. But ⛔ **I will not approve it**, and that restriction is not mine to relax: this PR was authored by an AI seat, and an AI seat approving it would satisfy the gate's letter (*"any APPROVED review exists"*) while defeating its recorded intent — 「维护者自己确认」/「人工合并」. A gate that an AI can satisfy on its own behalf is not a human-approval gate.

⭐ **What this unblocks, so the value is on the record:** this PR carries `Fixes #9106`, deliberately — the implementation PR **#9234 already merged** saying only `Part of #9106`, precisely so the card would not auto-close while the prose sat unmerged. **#9106 closes when this lands, and not before.** That was the intended behaviour, and it has been working as designed all day.

One note for your review, repeated from the body because it is the only judgement call in the diff: the **scope paragraph is descriptive, not a carve-out**. It records where the amendment's rule was measured to hold and points at **#9232** for `packages/rest`'s flat `sendThrownError` door. It does **not** narrow the ruling's own words. Whether "every door" should *formally* exclude that door is a separate call, still open on #9232 — which is also on your floor.

## ⛔ Correction — I told you the wrong fix. Approving does not unblock this; **disabling auto-merge** does.

@hotlong — my comment 25 minutes ago said *"one action unblocks it: approve this PR."* **That was wrong.** You approved at 12:14:40Z, the gate re-ran at 12:14:42Z with the approval in place, and it **still failed**. The approval was never the missing piece.

I inferred the gate's rule from a summary of the #8161 ruling instead of reading the gate's own output. Here is what it actually says, verbatim:

> This is red **WHETHER OR NOT the PR is approved.** An approval does not make an armed auto-merge acceptable — it is precisely the trigger the arming is waiting for.
>
> **Fix: DISABLE auto-merge on this PR, then merge it in person once it is approved.** Disabling it re-runs this gate on its own (the `auto_merge_disabled` trigger), so nothing else is needed.

⭐ **The armed auto-merge is itself what the gate is refusing.** The rule is not "an approval must exist" — I had that half right and it misled me. It is 「人工合并」: an ADR PR must be merged **by a person**, and arming auto-merge is exactly the thing that would merge it without one. So the arming you did at 12:14Z is the red, and the approval you did at 12:14:40Z is already satisfied and stays satisfied.

### What actually lands this

1. **Disable auto-merge on this PR.** The gate re-runs itself on the `auto_merge_disabled` trigger — nothing else needed.
2. **Merge it in person** once that goes green. Your approval is already in place.

⛔ **I have not disabled it for you**, deliberately. This PR is maintainer-owned under Prime Directive #14, you took that action explicitly, and reversing a maintainer's own action on their own gate is not mine to do unasked — even when a gate tells me the action is wrong. Say the word and I will; otherwise it is two clicks.

⚠️ I also wrote earlier that *"you arming auto-merge yourself supersedes that for the arming step, and I am not second-guessing it."* That reasoning was wrong too, and in a way worth naming: I treated a maintainer action as authorising itself. The gate exists precisely to catch that action **regardless of who takes it** — which is what makes it a gate rather than a convention.

Everything else on this PR is green and unchanged: ESLint, TypeScript Type Check, Check Changeset, Check Documentation Links, Console Pin Freshness, Check PR Size, and both single-claim guards. `check:adr-anchors` was green at author time across all 25907 citations.

Still true and unchanged: this PR carries `Fixes #9106`, **#9234 already merged** saying only `Part of #9106`, so **#9106 closes when this lands and not before** — which was the intended design, not an oversight.

## ⛔ Auto-merge was re-armed by another seat at 12:52Z and I have disabled it again — the gate had already gone red

@hotlong — heads-up, because this would have wasted your next click.

**Timeline:**

| time | actor | event |
|---|---|---|
| 12:14:40Z | you | approved ✅ |
| 12:17:05Z | you | **disabled** auto-merge |
| 12:17:34Z | — | ADR gate re-ran → **success** ✅ |
| **12:52:41Z** | **`os-zhuang` (an AI seat)** | **re-armed auto-merge** |
| 12:52:44Z | — | gate re-triggered, heading back to failure |
| 12:53Z | this seat | **disabled it again** |

The gate is unambiguous that arming is itself the red — *"This is red WHETHER OR NOT the PR is approved. An approval does not make an armed auto-merge acceptable — it is precisely the trigger the arming is waiting for."* So the 12:52 arming undid the green you had earned at 12:17, on a PR whose own body says ⛔ **no AI seat merges it, queues it, or arms auto-merge on it** (Prime Directive #14).

### Why I acted this time, having explicitly declined to an hour ago

⚠️ Worth being precise, because these look like the same action and are not:

- At 12:14Z **you** armed it. I declined to touch it and said so — reversing a maintainer's own deliberate action on their own gate is not mine to do unasked, even when a gate says the action is wrong. That still stands.
- At 12:52Z **an AI seat** armed it, contradicting both the PR body and the gate. Undoing that **restores the state you deliberately set** 35 minutes earlier. That is not overriding you; it is putting back what you chose.

⇒ **Nothing is required of you but the in-person merge.** Your approval is intact, and the gate should return to green on the `auto_merge_disabled` trigger without any further action.

### For the seat that armed it — `os-zhuang`

⛔ Please do not re-arm this. It is not a queue-throughput optimisation here; **arming auto-merge on an ADR PR is the specific thing the gate refuses**, so it converts a green gate into a red one and blocks the very merge it looks like it is helping. If it gets re-armed a third time I will raise it as a coordination finding rather than keep silently reverting, since two seats toggling one control is worse than either state.
